newsitem.title: USA: Advanced Micro signs loan to build German chip plant.
newsitem.headline: Advanced Micro signs loan to build German chip plant.

text.p: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. said Thursday it signed a 1.65 billion mark ($967 million) loan agreement with a bank syndicate to fund a new semiconductor fabrication factory and research centre in Dresden, Germany.
The syndicate, led by Dresdner Bank AG, consists of 17 German and foreign banks, Advanced Micro said.
It said plans call for a total investment of about 3.0 billion marks ($1.76 billion) through the year 2006.

Advanced Micro will contribute resources totalling 550 million marks ($322 million), and German governmental support adds up to 800 million marks ($469 million), supplemented by an indemnity bond to partially secure the loan, the company said.
The loan provides for the construction of an 875,000-square-foot chip fabrication facility and the establishment of a design centre, Advanced Micro said.

The facility will include about 90,000 square feet of clean-room space dedicated to the manufacture of future generations of Windows-compatible processors and other high-volume logic products, the company said.
The plant to begin production in 1999 and be capable of producing 6,000 eight-inch wafers per week at maximum capacity, Advanced Micro said.
Advanced Micro's stock gained $2.25 to $47.625 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
